The paper presents a two-scale optimization approach for designing graded lattice structures.
The approach combines asymptotic homogenization with a worst-case model for buckling load factors.
The worst-case model acts as a safeguard against pure local buckling.
The proposed approach can handle arbitrary microstructures.
The approach is limited to sizing problems with a lower bound on the lattice density.
A lattice consisting of equilateral triangles is used as the numerical example.
The proposed approach can effectively design graded lattice structures with improved global and local buckling resistance.
The computational effort is reduced compared to full-scale analyses.
The approach can be applied to various fields, including thermal management, energy absorption, and biomedical engineering.
The paper uses a worst-case model for buckling load factors.
The approach is based on asymptotic homogenization.
The paper presents a novel approach to include upscaled properties on the macroscopic scale.
The approach uses a piecewise cubic interpolation scheme.
The paper presents a numerical example to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.
The approach can be extended to non-linear regimes.
The paper presents a two-dimensional setting in this article to keep notations simple.
The approach can be extended to three-dimensional settings.
